chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali bin 'Aqaba, from Abu Jaroud, al-Mundhir al-Kindi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The most difficult of acts are three: Fairness towards people from yourself, until you are not pleased for yourself, from them, with anything except that you are pleased for them, from yourself, likewise; your consolation with a brother with regards to property; and mentioning Allah in all cases.

It is not (to say) «Glory be to Allah, and Praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is Greater» only, however, (it is that) whenever something comes to you which Allah has ordered to, you take it, and when something comes to you which Allah has forbidden, you abandon it.
ai.seo_question: What are the three most difficult acts of worship and how is true remembrance of Allah defined?
ai.summary: In Ma'ani al-Akhbar, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three rigorous acts as the pinnacle of spiritual discipline, linking internal self-accounting with external social justice. The narration deepens the concept of *dhikr* by defining it not merely as verbal invocation but as the active embodiment of divine will—observing commands and shunning prohibitions in every moment. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on the unity of belief and action, where true remembrance manifests in ethical conduct and material generosity.
